findings.reason: the builder cannot implement both the plain line and the multiple-leaned line, so the hold boundary the section asserts is undetermined until the prose and the done-when agree.
findings.text: the `--drain-by` form applies "the configured multiple ... as the usual lean on the increment" yet concludes "The remaining budget is therefore spread evenly so it lands at 100% at the target" — a lean above 1 on the increment reaches 100% before the target, so the two clauses cannot both hold, and the done-when at :1954 specifies the hold boundary as the plain "straight line to 100% at its target" without the multiple, disagreeing with the mechanism table.

findings.reason: without declaring the `budget.lift` block (or stating the two ceilings as code constants rather than config) the section enforces limits no operator can set, which is exactly the defect the bookend-reserve paragraph was added to close.
findings.text: the lift record's `pace_multiple` "must not exceed `budget.lift.max_multiple`" (:1910) and a lift is in force only when "now is before `granted_at + budget.lift.max_hours`" (:1919), but `reckon/schema/flight.yaml`'s `BudgetConfig` declares no `lift` block, so with `extra="forbid"` neither key can be set by any layer — the same undeclared-key defect §10 fixes one paragraph later for `bookend_reserve_pct`.

findings.reason: the decision rationale is the record of what the lead locked and now misstates the withheld amount and the number of reserves a lift releases, so the plan states two different rules for the same lift.
findings.text: the locked decision `lift-scope`'s rationale says "the unspent 8% comes from the locked resume reserve (5%) and the coordinator reserve (3%) ... releases both reserves", but §10 now names a third reserve and says "all three reserves read zero" (:1937) with "Up to a fifth of each metered window therefore expires unspent" (:1924) — the decision rationale names two reserves and an 8% remainder where the section body names three and a fifth.
